title: Pointer paths in an address space
hints: Store each region as its start, its bytes and whether it is static. A read of `size` bytes at `address` fits a region when `address >= start` and `address - start + size <= bytes.size()`; then build the value from the bytes, lowest first.

For the scan, go through `staticPointerSlots()`. Depth 1 is "is the pointer in this slot a little below the target?". Depth 2 is the same question asked of every pointer stored in the first `maxOffset` bytes of the object the slot points at.
requirements: Reads never cross a region boundary and fail cleanly outside mapped memory.
Paths resolve with a null and bounds check at every step.
The scan finds every depth-1 and depth-2 path within the offset limit, and nothing else.
Results come in a stable, documented order.
stretch: Add a `rebase` test: map the same image at a different start (as ASLR would) and show that a path stored as "image start + slot offset" still resolves, while a path stored as an absolute heap address does not.
